title: If, Elif, and Else
description: Make your program do different things depending on whether a condition is True.

content.text: If it is raining, you take an umbrella. Otherwise, you leave it at home. Programs make choices the same way.

items.sub: Run this block only when its **condition** (a True or False question like `score >= 10`) is True.
Short for "else if". Another condition to try.
What to do when nothing above was True.

content.question: What does an `if` need after the keyword?
options: A condition that is True or False
content.explain: `if` checks a condition, a question whose answer is `True` or `False`, like `score >= 10`.

parts.label: condition
parts.note: A question with a True or False answer.

parts.label: colon
parts.note: Ends the line. It says: the block for this branch comes next.

items: Write `if`, a condition, then a colon `:`.
The **indented** lines below run only when the condition is True.
Add `else:` for what happens when it is False.
Exactly one of the two blocks runs, never both.
content.title: How it works

steps.note: Check the condition: is `5 >= 10`? No, it is `False`. So Python skips the indented line under `if`.
The condition was False, so Python jumps to `else`.

content.title: Follow the branch
content.outro: Line 3 never ran. Only one branch runs.

items.title: Works
items.text: Colon at the end, and the line below is indented.

items.title: Breaks
items.text: No colon and no indent. Python stops with an error.

content.title: Colon and indent
content.caption: End each `if`, `elif` and `else` line with a colon, and indent the lines below it. The indent tells Python which lines belong to that branch.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: `12 > 10` is True, so the `if` block runs and the `else` block is skipped.

items: More than two outcomes? Add `elif` branches in between.
It runs the **first** branch that is True, then skips the rest.

content.value: Turn the dial below to see which branch wins for each score.

steps.note: Is `7 >= 10`? No. Skip the Gold block.
Try the `elif`: is `7 >= 5`? Yes, it is True.

content.title: Which branch wins?
content.outro: A branch was True, so `else` is skipped. Python never even looks at it.

content.question: What does this print when `score` is `3`?
content.explain: `3 >= 10` is False and `3 >= 5` is False, so neither branch runs and `else` does.

items: Python stops at the **first** True branch.
So the order of your conditions can change the answer.
Put the strictest condition at the top.

items.title: Wrong order
items.text: 12 is also 5 or more, so Silver wins and the Gold check is never reached.

items.title: Right order
items.text: The strictest check comes first, so 12 gets Gold.

content.caption: Swap the two checks to fix it.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: `35 > 20` is True first, so Python prints `Warm` and skips the `elif`, even though `35 > 30` is also True.

practice.question: The score below is 3, so it prints 'Bronze!'. Add an elif that prints 'Silver!' when the score is 5 or more.
This chain is in the wrong order, so a temp of 35 prints the wrong message. Swap the two conditions to fix it.

quiz.question: What does 'elif' stand for in Python?
quiz.explain: elif is short for 'else if'. It checks another condition when the branches above it turned out False.

quiz.question: What must you put at the end of an 'if' line?
quiz.explain: Every if line ends with a colon. It tells Python that the indented block below belongs to that if.

quiz.question: If two conditions in a chain are both True, which one runs?
quiz.explain: Python checks from top to bottom and stops at the first True condition. The rest are never checked.
